# About the author {-}

```{r author-photo, echo = FALSE, out.width = if (knitr::is_latex_output()) "35%" else "220px", fig.align = if (knitr::is_latex_output()) "center" else "default", fig.alt = "Portrait of Okan Bulut"}
knitr::include_graphics("images/okan-bulut.jpg")
```

**Okan Bulut** is a Professor of Measurement, Evaluation, and Data Science at
the University of Alberta. His work sits where artificial intelligence meets
educational measurement, data mining and learning analytics, and it asks a
practical question: How can assessments learn about the learner while the
learner is learning?

His research uses AI-driven algorithms and natural language processing to
build digital assessment systems that adapt to learners' preferences,
cognitive styles and performance over time. A large part of that work is
about scale: Generating test items automatically, scoring open-ended
responses automatically, and giving every student timely, useful feedback,
not just the few whose work a teacher has time to mark by hand.

He works closely with international research teams, school districts and
professional organizations to advance the responsible and ethical use of AI
in education, and partners with industry and regulatory bodies to turn
advances in psychometrics and learning analytics into practical assessment
and feedback systems that support better educational decisions.

At the University of Alberta he teaches courses in educational measurement,
assessment, computational psychometrics and machine learning, and he gives
workshops on computational techniques, programming and data visualization.
This book grew out of that teaching. mirtverse, the R package used
throughout, is his attempt to make modern item response theory as
approachable in the classroom as it is powerful in research.
